_doc: Revert-verify for the release gate (issue #4488): Auto Release must be gated on the REQUIRED-check SET read from the API at run time, not on the whole CI run's verdict — and a release skipped at a green required set must go RED (the issue's second acceptance item). Axes D1-D22 live in release-required-gate.test.ts; the subject is the gate script itself, driven as a process against a local stand-in API via GITHUB_API_URL. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this spec> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout. Recorded runs: see the PR body.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/.github/scripts/release-required-gate.mjs

M1_vacuous_green_on_empty_required._why: The shape `ci-watch.py` had to guard after a transient protection 403: with an empty required set, 'nothing failing and nothing missing' is VACUOUSLY true, so the gate would publish on every run. D6/D7/D8 are the fail-open floor — an unreadable set must fall back to the OLD predicate and say so, never read as green.
M1_vacuous_green_on_empty_required._note: D8 was predicted from the THEME ('a vacuous green') and dropped out: it exercises the OTHER canary — required set NON-empty, check-run listing empty — which is a separate branch this mutation never reaches. D8 is locked by M1b instead (integration-test-revert-verify §A44: read why the axis did not execute, do not re-point the expectation).

M3_unknown_conclusion_as_pass._why: A GATE has no later poll, so an unknown conclusion must block rather than be read as green (unlike a WATCHER, where 'keep waiting' is harmless). D10 feeds `stale`, a real check-run conclusion outside the PASS set.
M3_unknown_conclusion_as_pass._note: D2 reddens too, and that is the mutation being WIDER than its theme rather than a defect: collapsing every completed conclusion to `pass` also makes a required `failure` satisfied, which is exactly what D2 asserts against. Recorded instead of silently widened.

M4_first_not_latest_check_run._why: A stale RED shadowing a re-run's GREEN would block releases silently — the same class of silence this gate exists to remove. D11 supplies one name twice with the failure first.

M5_required_list_hardcoded._why: The defect the DERIVATION exists against: a hardcoded context list passes every green/red axis forever and silently stops gating on any newly added required check. The list here is even CORRECT for today, so only D12 — which asserts the branch object was actually read — can see it.

M5_required_list_hardcoded._note: D6/D7 redden because the hardcoded stub returns a context list UNCONDITIONALLY, so the scenarios that make the set empty/unreadable can no longer reach the gate — their inputs are swallowed upstream. That is the same class of blindness the mutant models (a list that stops tracking protection), observed on two more axes.

M6_missing_context_counts_as_satisfied._why: 'The required check produced no run' is not 'the required check passed' — treating it so would release on a run where a required job never started. D3 removes one required context from the listing.

M7_audit_swallows_the_silent_skip._why: The issue's second acceptance item, inverted: with this mutation a release skipped at a green required set stays GREEN — exactly the silence (#4488 is `skipped`, not `failure`, so no sweep of red runs sees it) the detector exists to break.
M7_audit_swallows_the_silent_skip._note: ⛔ The first version of this mutant changed only the verdict STRING to `SILENT-SKIP-IGNORED`, which still CONTAINS `SILENT-SKIP`; the axis asserts the substring and the rc, so nothing reddened and it read as 'the axis does not discriminate'. Anchored on the PAIR (message + decision) and mutating the DECISION (integration-test-revert-verify §A46).

M8_check_runs_page_one_only._why: A required context falling off page 1 reads as 'missing' and blocks the release quietly. D13 puts 140 filler runs ahead of the required ones so a non-paging gate judges none of them.

M9_audit_cries_wolf_on_transient._why: A red run on every transient 403 would train the reader to ignore this job, which is how a detector dies. D20 asserts the unjudged outcome keeps its OWN name and stays green.

M10_pending_as_pass._why: Releasing while a required check is still running publishes an unvalidated main. D4 leaves one required check `in_progress` with conclusion null.

M1b_empty_check_runs_still_judged._why: The canary on the OTHER input: with a non-empty required set and an EMPTY check-run listing every context reads as 'missing', which is indistinguishable from a transport failure. Judging that as a plain `false` would publish a verdict built on an empty measurement (self-satisfying-metric-weak-verifier §A7).

M2_no_cache_header_dropped._why: MEASURED 2026-10-01: the same Actions listing URL served a window 12 days stale until asked not to cache. D14 asserts the header at the SERVER — what was received — so dropping it on the wire cannot pass. Kept for cost asymmetry (free vs a false release verdict), not for a measured rate; see the script's `api()` header.
